summary: "Three Men in a Boat (To Say Nothing of the Dog)" by Jerome K. Jerome is a humorous novel published in 1889. Three friends and a dog embark on a two-week boating holiday up the Thames from Kingston to Oxford. What begins as a planned travel guide transforms into a comic masterpiece filled with misadventures, digressive anecdotes, and witty observations about everything from camping disasters to fishing mishaps. The humor remains fresh over a century later, capturing the timeless absurdities of friendship, leisure, and the great British pastime of muddling through.
